To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the life-cycle locational behavior of households depends upon their ability to use regional amenities.

The ability to use a regional amenity is a function of the accumulation of human capital specific to that amenity, and the interaction of this amenity-specific human-capital with regional wage rates, determines the timing of locational moves in the working period of life as well the retirement period.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the life-cycle model of locational choice provides an explanation of the timing of moves and a mechanism for explaining observed heterogeneity in the timing and duration of residence.
the interaction of the life-cycle model with regional amenity differences is sufficient to explain the observed locational behavior of households.
the interaction between regional amenities and human capital is a powerful force in explaining locational choice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the timing of moves is not random.
the interaction of the accumulation of human capital and regional amenities can explain the timing of household locational decisions in ways that other models cannot.
life-cycle locational choice is not simply a choice between regions but a choice between the amenities and other characteristics of the regions.
